heroSub: 11 Lopburi hotels picked across every budget — an old-town resort within walking distance of the train station, drive-friendly new-town hotels, a stay on the Asia Highway, all the way to a resort by the Pa Sak Cholasit Dam. Covers the old town, new town, and the Phatthana Nikhom side. From ฿350–1,500/night.
heroStats: 🏨 3 main zones (Old Town · New Town · Pa Sak Dam)
introH2: 🐒 Why does your choice of area matter in Lopburi?
introHtml: Lopburi is a history-and-monkeys town — most people come to see the monkeys, pay respects at Phra Prang Sam Yot, and walk King Narai's Palace. Accommodation splits into 3 sides, each with a different feel — the Old Town has Phra Prang Sam Yot, Prang Sam Yot's monkeys at San Phra Kan, King Narai's Palace, and the train station; great if you arrive by train or want to walk everywhere. The New Town (Tha Sala–Tha Hin–Khao Sam Yot) has Big C, malls, restaurants, and roomy parking; best if you drive. And the Phatthana Nikhom–Pa Sak Cholasit Dam side is about 50–60 minutes out, good for the dam and the sunflower fields. Many people book without checking the zone and then spend the whole day driving back and forth. This guide rounds up 11 Lopburi hotels picked across every tier, each with real guest reviews, prices compared on 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Lopburi has no metro and no commercial airport — its strength is the northern-line train station right in the old town, with many Bangkok–North services stopping here, so plenty of travellers arrive by train and walk straight into the old town. Pick your zone around your plan: Old Town (Tha Hin–Pa Tan) — walk to Phra Prang Sam Yot, San Phra Kan (the monkeys), King Narai's Palace, and the train station; ideal without a car. New Town (Tha Sala–Khao Sam Yot) — near Big C, malls, restaurants, and big car parks; ideal if you drive. Phatthana Nikhom–Pa Sak Cholasit Dam — about 50–60 minutes from town, good for the dam and sunflower fields. Almost every new-town hotel has free parking, so it suits road-trippers.

entries.storyHtml: Windsor Resort is the most-reviewed hotel in this guide, with 870 reviews at a solid 8.0 · Its strength is the old-town location in Pa Tan — within walking distance of the train station and close to King Narai's Palace, ideal if you arrive by train to see the monkeys without a car · The European-themed building is a fun touch, rooms are spacious and clean, there are free bikes and free parking, and rates start at just ฿580, making it a great-value base for exploring the old town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Some rooms catch train noise since it's near the station — if you're a light sleeper, ask for a Resort Zone room on the inner side, away from the tracks.
pros: Most reviewed in this guide (870) — very reliable data
Walk to the train station, near King Narai's Palace
Fun European-themed building, spacious clean rooms
Free bikes and free parking, from just ฿580
cons: Some rooms catch train noise near the station

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate and can change by date and season — always check live rates and compare 3 sites before booking · During the King Narai Reign Fair (February) and the sunflower season (late–early year), rooms fill fast, especially in the old town and on the Pa Sak Dam side, so book 2–4 weeks ahead · Lopburi has no metro or commercial airport, but there's a northern-line train station in the old town — you can take a train from Bangkok and walk straight into Monkey City · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about Lopburi hotels

faq.q: ❓ Which area is best to stay in Lopburi?
faq.a: It depends on your plan and whether you have a car · The Old Town (Tha Hin–Pa Tan) is walking distance to Phra Prang Sam Yot, San Phra Kan (the monkeys), King Narai's Palace, and the train station — ideal without a car (Windsor Resort, Noom Guesthouse) · The New Town (Tha Sala–Khao Sam Yot) is near Big C, malls, restaurants, and big car parks — ideal if you drive (The Charlotte, Lopburi Inn Resort, Grand Lopburi, JRD, Benjatara, HOP INN) · Phatthana Nikhom–Pa Sak Cholasit Dam is about 50–60 minutes out, good for the dam and sunflowers (Mourakot Resort)

faq.q: ❓ How much do Lopburi hotels cost?
faq.a: Lopburi is very wallet-friendly: guesthouses and budget stays start around ฿350–520 (Noom Guesthouse, Phetlada, Benjatara) · 3-star hotels and boutiques run about ฿580–900 (Windsor, HOP INN, The Charlotte, Grand, JRD, Mourakot, Lopburi Inn Hotel) · the 4-star resort with a pool starts around ฿900–1,500 (Lopburi Inn Resort)

faq.q: ❓ Arriving by train — where can I stay within walking distance?
faq.a: Lopburi has a northern-line train station in the old town, with many Bangkok–North services stopping here · Stays within walking distance or near the station are Windsor Resort (walk to the station, near King Narai's Palace) and Noom Guesthouse (a wooden house in the heart of the old town, walk to Phra Prang Sam Yot and the monkeys) — ideal without a car if you arrive by train and want to explore the old town on foot

faq.q: ❓ Which Lopburi hotel has a swimming pool?
faq.a: In this guide, the one with a pool is Lopburi Inn Resort, the only 4-star here, with an outdoor pool and spacious rooms, many with pool-view balconies — ideal for families with kids, from ฿900 · Most other Lopburi stays have no pool, so pick this one if a pool is a must

faq.q: ❓ Want to visit the Pa Sak Cholasit Dam — where should I stay?
faq.a: If you're set on the Pa Sak Dam and the sunflower fields, stay on the Phatthana Nikhom side · Mourakot Resort ฿700 has garden bungalows near the dam in a quiet rural setting, with easy driving access · It's about 50–60 minutes from town, so you'll want a car, and shops nearby are few — stock up on food in town first

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a Lopburi hotel?
faq.a: On regular weekdays, 1–2 weeks ahead is plenty since Lopburi isn't crowded · But during the King Narai Reign Fair (February) and the sunflower season (late–early year), old-town and Pa Sak Dam stays fill very fast — book 2–4 weeks ahead or more
